# Linear Vibration Motor: Structural Design and Functional Overview

## Core Structural Components

The linear vibration motor is fundamentally composed of four main structural elements: a housing, a stator, a vibrator, and an elastic support member. These components work in concert to form a complete electromechanical system capable of generating precise vibrational feedback. The housing serves as the outer protective enclosure, providing structural integrity and containing all internal components, while the elastic support member enables the necessary mechanical compliance for oscillatory motion.

## Vibrator and Stator Composition

The vibrator, which is the moving element responsible for generating vibration, is composed of a mass block combined with magnets. The mass block provides the inertial component necessary for vibration generation, while the magnets create the magnetic field required for electromagnetic actuation.

The stator, in contrast, remains stationary and includes coils along with circuit boards. The coils serve as the electromagnetic driving elements, while the circuit boards provide the necessary electrical connections and control pathways to energize the coils in a coordinated manner.

## Coil Arrangement and Mounting Configuration

A key design feature of this motor is the dual-coil arrangement: a first coil and a second coil are positioned on opposite sides of the mass block. This symmetrical placement allows for balanced electromagnetic force generation, contributing to more controlled and efficient vibrational output. Each of these coils is connected to its own dedicated coil fixing board, ensuring stable positioning and preventing unwanted movement during operation.

The mounting hierarchy continues with the first and second coil fixing boards being mounted onto separate washer boards. These washer boards, in turn, are fixed directly to the motor housing. This layered mounting approach—coil to fixing board, fixing board to washer board, washer board to housing—creates a secure and stable overall assembly, ensuring that all components maintain precise alignment during motor operation.

## Design Advantages and Functional Benefits

This carefully engineered structural arrangement yields significant performance benefits. By optimizing the positioning and mounting of the coils relative to the magnets and mass block, the design effectively reduces magnetic field loss that might otherwise occur due to misalignment or inefficient spatial arrangement. Consequently, this configuration improves magnetic field utilization efficiency, allowing the motor to convert electrical energy into mechanical vibration with greater effectiveness.

Ultimately, this optimized design enables the motor to deliver reliable and responsive vibration feedback for user touch operations, making it well-suited for applications in consumer electronics, wearable devices, and other systems requiring precise haptic feedback mechanisms.

# Linear Vibration Motor for Touch Feedback Applications

## Technical Field

The present disclosure relates to the field of vibration motor technology, and more particularly to a linear vibration motor designed for providing haptic (touch) feedback in electronic devices such as smartphones, tablets, wearable devices, and other touch-screen-enabled apparatus requiring precise and efficient vibrational response.

## Background

With the rapid development of touch-screen technology, users increasingly rely on tactile feedback mechanisms to confirm touch operations, button presses, and interactive gestures on their electronic devices. Linear vibration motors have become a critical component in delivering this feedback due to their ability to generate consistent, rapid, and controllable vibrations. However, conventional vibration motor designs often suffer from inefficiencies in magnetic field utilization, resulting in energy loss, reduced vibration amplitude, and suboptimal feedback performance. There exists a need for an improved linear vibration motor structure that maximizes magnetic field efficiency while maintaining a compact and reliable design suitable for integration into modern electronic devices.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention provides a linear vibration motor structure specifically engineered to address the aforementioned shortcomings in the art. The motor comprises four primary structural components: a housing, a stator assembly, a vibrator assembly, and an elastic support member, each configured to work in concert to produce efficient and effective vibrational feedback.

### Housing

The housing serves as the outer protective structure of the linear vibration motor, providing mechanical support and enclosure for the internal components. It defines an internal cavity within which the stator, vibrator, and elastic support member are accommodated. The housing is designed to maintain structural integrity while allowing sufficient space for the vibrator to oscillate freely along its intended axis of motion.

### Stator Assembly

The stator assembly is fixedly mounted within the housing and constitutes a critical element in the generation of the magnetic driving force. The stator comprises two separate fixing boards, each of which supports one of two coils—designated as the first coil and the second coil, respectively. These coils are electrically driven to generate alternating magnetic fields that interact with the magnetic components of the vibrator.

In addition to the fixing boards, the stator assembly further includes washer boards that are attached to the housing. These washer boards serve to properly position and secure the coils and fixing boards within the housing, ensuring precise alignment between the stator's magnetic field-generating components and the vibrator's magnetic elements. The washer boards also assist in maintaining consistent spacing and structural stability during the vibration motor's operation.

### Vibrator Assembly

The vibrator assembly comprises a mass block and one or more magnets affixed to or integrated within the mass block. The mass block is configured to move linearly within the housing in response to the alternating magnetic fields generated by the first and second coils. The magnets on the vibrator are strategically positioned to interact directly with the corresponding coils mounted on the separate fixing boards, thereby creating an electromagnetic driving force that induces linear oscillation of the vibrator.

The dual-coil configuration—wherein the first coil and second coil are mounted separately on distinct fixing boards—allows for a more effective magnetic circuit design. This arrangement enables the magnets of the vibrator to interact with both coils simultaneously or in a coordinated sequence, thereby enhancing the overall electromagnetic coupling efficiency between the stator and vibrator components.

### Elastic Support Member

The elastic support member is disposed between the vibrator and the housing (or between the vibrator and the stator assembly) to provide restoring force to the vibrator after each vibrational cycle. This elastic component ensures that the vibrator returns to its equilibrium position following displacement, enabling sustained and repeatable oscillatory motion. The elastic support member also contributes to the overall resonant characteristics of the motor, allowing it to operate efficiently at its designed vibration frequency.

## Technical Advantages

The configuration described above—wherein the vibrator's mass block and magnets interact with dual coils mounted on separate fixing boards and washer boards attached to the housing—offers several significant technical advantages over conventional single-coil or integrated-coil vibration motor designs:

**1. Reduced Magnetic Field Loss:** By separating the first and second coils onto distinct fixing boards, the magnetic flux paths are optimized, minimizing the dissipation or leakage of magnetic field energy that commonly occurs in designs where coils share a single mounting structure or are positioned suboptimally relative to the vibrator's magnets.

**2. Improved Magnetic Field Utilization Efficiency:** The dual-coil, dual-fixing-board arrangement allows for more precise alignment between the coils and the magnets of the vibrator, ensuring that a greater proportion of the generated magnetic field is effectively converted into linear mechanical motion. This results in stronger and more consistent vibration output for a given electrical input, improving the motor's overall energy efficiency.

**3. Enhanced Structural Stability:** The use of washer boards attached to the housing provides additional mechanical support and precise positioning for the fixing boards and coils, reducing the likelihood of misalignment during manufacturing, assembly, or prolonged use. This contributes to the long-term reliability and consistent performance of the vibration motor.

**4. Effective Vibration Feedback Delivery:** As a direct result of the improvements in magnetic field utilization and structural design, the linear vibration motor is capable of delivering more immediate, pronounced, and reliable vibrational feedback in response to user touch operations. This enhanced feedback performance is particularly beneficial in applications such as touch-screen interfaces, where users depend on tactile responses to confirm successful input registration.

## Conclusion

In summary, the disclosed linear vibration motor represents a significant advancement in vibration motor design for touch feedback applications. Through the strategic separation of coils onto individual fixing boards, combined with the use of washer boards for precise positioning within the housing, the motor achieves reduced magnetic field loss and improved magnetic field utilization efficiency. These technical improvements translate directly into superior vibration feedback performance, making the disclosed motor structure highly suitable for integration into a wide range of touch-sensitive electronic devices requiring reliable and efficient haptic feedback mechanisms.

# Patent Claim Draft

## Title
**Linear Vibration Motor with Dual-Coil Configuration and Washer Board Assembly for Enhanced Magnetic Field Utilization**

---

## Field of the Invention

This invention relates to linear vibration motors, and more particularly to a linear resonant actuator (LRA) employing a dual-coil arrangement in cooperation with ferromagnetic washer boards to improve magnetic flux linkage, increase electromagnetic force output, and enhance overall vibration efficiency while maintaining a compact form factor.

---

## Background

Conventional linear vibration motors typically utilize a single coil and magnet assembly, where a significant portion of the generated magnetic field is not effectively coupled to the coil, resulting in energy loss and reduced vibration amplitude for a given input power. There exists a need for a motor structure that more efficiently channels magnetic flux to maximize force generation without increasing the overall size or power consumption of the device.

---

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention provides a linear vibration motor comprising a vibrating mass with an embedded magnet assembly, a stationary dual-coil structure, and one or more washer boards constructed from high-permeability magnetic material. The washer boards are positioned to guide and concentrate magnetic flux lines through the dual coils, thereby increasing the effective magnetic field density within the coil regions and improving the electromagnetic-to-mechanical energy conversion efficiency of the motor.

---

## Claims

**Claim 1.**
A linear vibration motor comprising:
a housing defining an internal cavity;
a vibrating mass movably disposed within the internal cavity, the vibrating mass comprising a magnet assembly having at least one permanent magnet with a defined polarity orientation;
a dual-coil assembly fixed relative to the housing, the dual-coil assembly comprising a first coil and a second coil arranged in a spaced-apart configuration along an axis of vibration, each coil being electrically connected to a drive circuit configured to induce oscillating current therein;
at least one washer board disposed adjacent to the dual-coil assembly, the washer board formed from a ferromagnetic material and configured to guide magnetic flux generated by the magnet assembly through the first coil and the second coil to increase magnetic field utilization within the coil regions;
and an elastic support member coupling the vibrating mass to the housing, the elastic support member configured to permit reciprocating linear motion of the vibrating mass along the axis of vibration in response to electromagnetic force generated by interaction between the magnet assembly and the dual-coil assembly.

**Claim 2.**
The linear vibration motor of claim 1, wherein the at least one washer board comprises a first washer board positioned adjacent to the first coil and a second washer board positioned adjacent to the second coil, each washer board defining a central aperture configured to permit passage of the magnet assembly during vibration.

**Claim 3.**
The linear vibration motor of claim 1, wherein the first coil and the second coil are wound in opposite winding directions relative to one another such that current flowing through the drive circuit generates magnetic fields of complementary polarity in the first coil and the second coil.

**Claim 4.**
The linear vibration motor of claim 1, wherein the magnet assembly comprises a first magnet and a second magnet arranged with opposing polarities along the axis of vibration, the first magnet being positioned to interact primarily with the first coil and the second magnet being positioned to interact primarily with the second coil.

**Claim 5.**
The linear vibration motor of claim 1, wherein the washer board comprises a silicon steel material or a soft magnetic alloy having a magnetic permeability greater than a threshold value sufficient to reduce magnetic flux leakage outside of the dual-coil assembly.

**Claim 6.**
The linear vibration motor of claim 1, wherein the washer board further comprises a plurality of radially extending flux-guiding protrusions configured to direct magnetic flux lines toward a central axis of the dual-coil assembly.

**Claim 7.**
The linear vibration motor of claim 1, wherein the elastic support member comprises at least one spring element coupled between the vibrating mass and an interior wall of the housing, the spring element being configured to establish a resonant frequency of the linear vibration motor.

**Claim 8.**
The linear vibration motor of claim 1, wherein the drive circuit is configured to supply an alternating current to the first coil and the second coil at a frequency substantially matching a mechanical resonant frequency of the vibrating mass and elastic support member.

**Claim 9.**
The linear vibration motor of claim 1, wherein the washer board is positioned to form a closed magnetic flux path in cooperation with the magnet assembly, the housing, and the dual-coil assembly, thereby reducing magnetic reluctance within the motor.

**Claim 10.**
A method of manufacturing a linear vibration motor, the method comprising:
providing a housing;
disposing a dual-coil assembly comprising a first coil and a second coil within the housing;
positioning at least one washer board formed from a ferromagnetic material adjacent to the dual-coil assembly to guide magnetic flux through the first coil and the second coil;
disposing a vibrating mass comprising a magnet assembly within the housing such that the magnet assembly is movable relative to the dual-coil assembly along an axis of vibration; and
coupling the vibrating mass to the housing via an elastic support member configured to permit reciprocating linear motion of the vibrating mass.

**Claim 11.**
The linear vibration motor of claim 1, further comprising a damping member disposed within the internal cavity to reduce mechanical noise generated during operation of the vibrating mass.

**Claim 12.**
The linear vibration motor of claim 2, wherein the first washer board and the second washer board are magnetically coupled to a housing wall formed from a ferromagnetic material to further enhance magnetic flux utilization.

---

## Detailed Description (Excerpt)

In one embodiment, the dual-coil assembly is positioned symmetrically about a midpoint of the vibrating mass's travel path, with the first coil and second coil each surrounding a portion of the central shaft along which the magnet assembly translates. The washer boards, positioned at opposite ends of the dual-coil assembly, act as flux concentrators, directing magnetic field lines that would otherwise dissipate into the surrounding housing structure back through the active coil windings.

This configuration increases the effective flux density experienced by each coil by an amount dependent on the permeability of the washer board material and its geometric proximity to the coil windings, resulting in improved force output per unit of input current (higher motor constant, K_t) compared to single-coil designs lacking flux-guiding structures.

The dual-coil arrangement further enables differential driving schemes, wherein the first coil and second coil may be driven with phase-offset or amplitude-modulated signals to fine-tune the force waveform applied to the vibrating mass, enabling customizable haptic feedback profiles.

---

*Note: This is a template/draft for illustrative purposes. Actual patent claims require careful drafting by a licensed patent attorney or agent, prior art analysis, and compliance with jurisdiction-specific patent office requirements (e.g., USPTO, EPO, CNIPA) to ensure claims are novel, non-obvious, and properly supported by the specification.*

# Technical Summary: Dual-Coil Linear Vibration Motor with Symmetric Mass Block Actuation

## Overview

This document describes the architectural configuration and functional components of a linear resonant actuator (LRA) employing a dual-coil electromagnetic drive system, wherein two independently or synchronously driven coils are positioned on opposing sides of a centrally suspended mass block to achieve bidirectional or enhanced unidirectional linear oscillation.

## Core Structural Components

### 1. Central Mass Block (Vibrating Element)
- **Function**: Serves as the primary inertial mass responsible for generating perceptible haptic vibration output.
- **Composition**: Typically constructed from a high-density material (e.g., tungsten alloy or steel) to maximize inertial force within a compact form factor.
- **Magnetic Configuration**: Houses one or more permanent magnets (commonly NdFeB - neodymium-iron-boron) affixed to or embedded within the mass, oriented to interact with the magnetic fields generated by the flanking coils.
- **Suspension**: Mechanically coupled to the housing via one or more springs (leaf springs, coil springs, or elastomeric supports) that constrain motion to a single linear axis and provide restoring force for resonant oscillation.

### 2. Dual Coil Assembly
- **Positioning**: Two electromagnetic coils are mounted on opposite ends of the motor housing, flanking the mass block symmetrically along the axis of motion.
- **Winding Configuration**: Each coil consists of enameled copper wire wound around a bobbin or core structure; polarity and winding direction are configured such that energizing both coils produces complementary (additive) magnetic forces acting on the mass block from both directions.
- **Electrical Configuration**: May be wired in series or parallel, or driven independently via separate terminals, depending on design intent (synchronized push-pull actuation vs. redundant/staged actuation).

### 3. Magnetic Circuit
- **Permanent Magnets**: Fixed to the mass block, providing the static magnetic field necessary for force generation via Lorentz force interaction with coil current.
- **Flux Path Components**: Often includes a yoke or pole piece structure (soft magnetic material, e.g., low-carbon steel) to concentrate and direct magnetic flux between each coil and the adjacent magnet pole face, minimizing flux leakage and maximizing electromagnetic coupling efficiency.

### 4. Mechanical Suspension System
- **Spring Elements**: Positioned at one or both ends of the mass block (or integrated laterally), these provide the mechanical restoring force that, combined with the mass, establishes the system's resonant frequency (f₀).
- **Guide Structures**: Rails, bushings, or flexure guides may be incorporated to prevent lateral or rotational motion, ensuring motion is constrained purely to the intended linear axis.

### 5. Housing and Enclosure
- **Outer Casing**: Provides structural rigidity, environmental protection, and precise alignment of the coil-magnet air gaps on both sides.
- **End Caps**: Anchor points for coil assemblies and spring termination points, often on opposite ends of the housing to maintain the symmetric dual-coil arrangement.

## Operating Principle

1. **Excitation**: An alternating current (AC) drive signal, typically sinusoidal or square-wave at or near the system's mechanical resonant frequency, is applied to the coil(s).
2. **Force Generation**: Current flowing through each coil generates a magnetic field that interacts with the permanent magnet(s) on the mass block, producing a Lorentz force (F = BIL) along the linear axis.
3. **Synchronized Actuation**: With coils on opposite sides, the driving signals are phased such that when one coil repels (or attracts) the mass in one direction, the opposite coil's field complements this motion—effectively doubling the usable stroke force compared to a single-coil design, or enabling redundant operation if one coil fails.
4. **Resonant Amplification**: The spring-mass system oscillates at its natural frequency, and driving near this frequency (f₀) maximizes vibration amplitude for a given input power via mechanical resonance amplification (Q-factor enhancement).
5. **Vibration Output**: The reciprocating motion of the mass block, transmitted through the housing, produces the perceptible vibration output at the motor's exterior mounting surface.

## Design Considerations

| Parameter | Consideration |
|---|---|
| **Air Gap Tolerance** | Both coil-magnet gaps must be precisely matched to ensure symmetric force output and prevent asymmetric vibration bias. |
| **Coil Impedance Matching** | Dual coils must be electrically balanced (matched resistance/inductance) if driven from a single source to avoid uneven force contribution. |
| **Resonant Frequency Tuning** | Spring constant (k) and mass (m) are selected per f₀ = (1/2π)√(k/m) to match target drive frequency (commonly 150–250 Hz for haptic applications). |
| **Thermal Management** | Dual coil operation may increase power dissipation; thermal design must account for heat generated by both windings, especially in continuous-duty scenarios. |
| **Damping** | Mechanical or eddy-current damping may be introduced to control settling time and reduce residual vibration ("ringing") after drive signal cessation. |

## Advantages of Dual-Coil Symmetric Configuration

- **Increased Force Output**: Simultaneous contribution from both coils increases peak force relative to single-coil designs of similar volume.
- **Improved Motion Symmetry**: Opposing coil placement helps balance forces on both halves of the oscillation cycle, reducing waveform distortion.
- **Redundancy**: In failure scenarios, a single functioning coil may sustain reduced but functional vibration output.
- **Design Flexibility**: Enables differential driving schemes (e.g., phase-shifted excitation) for waveform shaping in advanced haptic feedback applications.

A vibration motor for touch feedback applications in mobile devices is disclosed, comprising a housing, a stator assembly, and a vibrator assembly configured to reduce magnetic field loss and enhance vibration efficiency. The stator assembly includes a coil disposed on a circuit board and a magnetic circuit system comprising a yoke plate and at least one magnet arranged to form a closed magnetic loop. The vibrator assembly includes a mass block coupled to an elastic support member, wherein the mass block is positioned to interact with the magnetic field generated by the magnetic circuit system.

In one embodiment, the yoke plate is configured with an extended flange portion that substantially surrounds the magnet, thereby minimizing magnetic flux leakage and directing a greater proportion of the magnetic field toward the coil. This structural arrangement increases the effective magnetic flux density within the working air gap between the magnet and the coil, resulting in improved electromagnetic force generation for a given input current.

The vibration motor further includes a damping structure disposed between the vibrator assembly and the housing to reduce unwanted resonance and improve haptic response consistency. The elastic support member is configured with a specific stiffness coefficient that, in combination with the enhanced magnetic circuit, allows the motor to achieve a rapid start-up time and a shortened braking distance, thereby providing crisp, high-fidelity haptic feedback suitable for touchscreen applications.

The invention further provides a manufacturing method comprising the steps of assembling the yoke plate and magnet to form the closed magnetic circuit, mounting the coil on the circuit board within the housing, and coupling the mass block to the elastic support member such that the vibrator assembly is suspended within the magnetic field with minimal frictional loss.

The disclosed vibration motor achieves reduced power consumption, increased vibration amplitude, and enhanced durability compared to conventional linear resonant actuators, making it particularly suitable for integration into smartphones, tablets, wearable devices, and other portable electronic devices requiring precise and energy-efficient touch feedback mechanisms.

# Linear Resonant Actuator (LRA): Formal Technical Description

## 1. Overview

A Linear Resonant Actuator (LRA) is an electromechanical vibration device that generates haptic feedback through the oscillatory motion of a mass-spring system driven by electromagnetic force. The actuator operates at or near its mechanical resonant frequency to maximize output efficiency with minimal input power.

## 2. Core Structural Components

### 2.1 Stator Assembly

The stator serves as the stationary reference frame of the actuator and comprises:

- **Housing/Casing**: An outer shell (typically metal or engineering plastic) that encloses all internal components and provides mechanical protection and mounting interfaces to the host device.
- **Coil Assembly**: One or more electromagnetic coils wound around a bobbin or directly onto a support structure, fixed rigidly to the stator base or housing floor.
- **Fixing Board (PCB/FPC)**: A printed circuit board or flexible printed circuit that:
  - Provides electrical interconnection to the coil terminals via soldering or welding pads
  - Is mechanically bonded or riveted to the stator housing base
  - Routes power/signal traces to external connector pins or solder pads for system-level integration

### 2.2 Vibrator (Mover) Assembly

The vibrator is the moving mass responsible for generating vibration and includes:

- **Mass Block**: A high-density material (commonly tungsten alloy or steel) that provides the inertial mass required for the desired vibration amplitude.
- **Permanent Magnet(s)**: Mounted on or embedded within the mass block, positioned in direct magnetic coupling alignment with the stator coil(s), oriented to maximize Lorentz force interaction upon current excitation.
- **Yoke/Pole Piece (optional)**: A ferromagnetic structure that channels magnetic flux to enhance field concentration between the magnet and coil gap.

### 2.3 Elastic Support (Spring) System

The elastic support provides the restoring force that defines the resonant frequency and constrains vibrator motion to a single translational axis:

- **Spring Type**: Typically realized as metal leaf springs, coil springs, or elastomeric supports, symmetrically arranged (top and bottom, or left and right) relative to the vibrator.
- **Attachment Points**:
  - One end of each spring is fixed to the stator housing (top cover and/or base)
  - The opposite end is fixed to the vibrator mass block
- **Function**: Constrains the vibrator to reciprocating linear motion along the intended vibration axis while suppressing lateral, rotational, or off-axis displacement.

## 3. Assembly Configuration and Sequence

### 3.1 Stator Sub-Assembly Process

1. The coil is wound and terminated with lead wires or terminal pins.
2. The coil is seated into a designated slot or boss feature on the stator base (housing floor), ensuring concentric alignment with the intended magnetic gap axis.
3. The fixing board (PCB/FPC) is positioned adjacent to or beneath the coil.
4. Coil leads are electrically connected to the fixing board via soldering, thermal compression bonding, or conductive adhesive.
5. The fixing board is mechanically secured to the housing base using adhesive bonding, snap-fit features, or fasteners, ensuring the board remains flush and does not obstruct vibrator travel.

### 3.2 Vibrator Sub-Assembly Process

1. The permanent magnet is magnetized and bonded (typically via adhesive) to the mass block in the position aligned with the stator coil's magnetic axis.
2. If a yoke is used, it is assembled onto the magnet or mass block to close the magnetic circuit.
3. The completed vibrator sub-assembly is weighed and balanced to meet resonant frequency tolerance specifications.

### 3.3 Elastic Support Integration

1. Springs are affixed to the vibrator mass block at designated attachment points (via welding, adhesive, or mechanical crimping).
2. The vibrator, now fitted with springs, is lowered/inserted into the stator housing cavity such that the magnet aligns coaxially with the coil, maintaining a uniform air gap.
3. The free ends of the springs are fixed to corresponding features on the stator housing (base and/or top cover), establishing the suspension system.

### 3.4 Final Enclosure

1. The top cover is placed over the assembled stator-vibrator-spring system and joined to the housing base via laser welding, ultrasonic welding, or adhesive sealing.
2. The fixing board's external terminals remain exposed or routed through the housing wall for external electrical connection.

## 4. Operating Principle

Upon application of an alternating current (AC) signal at or near the system's natural resonant frequency to the stator coil, an alternating magnetic field is generated. This field interacts with the static magnetic field of the vibrator's permanent magnet, producing an alternating Lorentz force along the constrained motion axis. The elastic support system stores and releases mechanical energy each half-cycle, sustaining reciprocating oscillation of the vibrator mass with amplitude governed by the drive frequency's proximity to resonance, the system's damping coefficient, and the input drive voltage/current amplitude.

## 5. Key Design Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Resonant Frequency (f₀) | Determined by vibrator mass (m) and spring constant (k): f₀ = (1/2π)√(k/m) |
| Air Gap | Distance between magnet and coil/pole piece; affects electromagnetic coupling efficiency |
| Spring Constant (k) | Determined by spring material, thickness, geometry, and number of spring elements |
| Vibrator Mass (m) | Determines inertial force and directly influences resonant frequency and output amplitude |

---

Would you like this description formatted as a patent-style specification, a technical datasheet, or expanded with dimensional/tolerance specifications for a specific LRA form factor (e.g., cylindrical Z-axis or flat X/Y-axis type)?

# PATENT SPECIFICATION

## TITLE OF INVENTION
**Haptic Feedback Vibration Motor with Enhanced Magnetic Efficiency Structure**

---

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention relates to the field of vibration motors, and more particularly to a haptic feedback vibration motor employing a linear resonant actuator (LRA) architecture with an improved magnetic circuit design utilizing a housing assembly, mass block, magnet configuration, and dual coil fixing boards to enhance electromagnetic efficiency, reduce flux leakage, and improve overall vibration output while maintaining a compact form factor suitable for portable electronic devices.

---

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

[0002] Haptic feedback vibration motors are widely used in smartphones, wearable devices, gaming controllers, and other portable electronic products to provide tactile feedback to users. Conventional vibration motors typically employ a single coil and magnet arrangement, which suffers from several drawbacks including insufficient magnetic flux density, energy loss due to flux leakage, inconsistent vibration amplitude, and limited dynamic response.

[0003] Existing linear resonant actuators generally comprise a housing, a stationary coil assembly fixed to a base or bracket, and a movable mass block containing a magnet that oscillates along a defined axis under electromagnetic force. However, in single-coil designs, the magnetic circuit is often incomplete, resulting in substantial leakage flux that does not contribute to the driving force, thereby reducing overall motor efficiency and requiring higher input current to achieve desired vibration intensity.

[0004] Furthermore, conventional designs often suffer from mechanical instability of the coil structure during operation, leading to coil deformation, positional drift, and reduced reliability over the operational lifetime of the device. There remains a need in the art for an improved vibration motor structure that maximizes magnetic circuit efficiency, provides stable coil positioning, and delivers consistent, high-amplitude haptic feedback while minimizing power consumption and manufacturing complexity.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0005] The present invention provides a haptic feedback vibration motor comprising a housing defining an internal cavity, a mass block movably disposed within the housing and configured to oscillate along a vibration axis, at least one magnet assembly fixed to or embedded within the mass block, and a dual coil fixing board structure disposed on opposing sides of the magnet assembly to form an enhanced magnetic circuit.

[0006] In one aspect, the dual coil fixing board structure comprises a first coil fixing board and a second coil fixing board, each mounted with an electrically conductive coil, positioned symmetrically about the magnet assembly such that the magnetic flux generated by the magnet assembly is efficiently coupled with both coils simultaneously, thereby forming a closed or substantially closed magnetic loop that significantly reduces flux leakage compared to single-coil designs.

[0007] In another aspect, the housing comprises a magnetically permeable material configured to serve as a portion of the magnetic return path, further enhancing magnetic circuit efficiency by directing stray flux back through the effective working gap of the coils.

[0008] In yet another aspect, the mass block is supported by elastic members (springs) connected between the mass block and the housing, allowing the mass block to oscillate along the vibration axis in response to alternating current applied to the dual coils, generating a resonant vibration force that is transmitted to the housing and, consequently, to the host device.

[0009] The dual coil fixing board configuration further provides mechanical stability by rigidly securing the coils in fixed positions relative to the housing, preventing coil displacement or deformation during high-frequency, high-amplitude oscillation, thereby improving the reliability and consistency of the haptic output over the operational life of the device.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

### General Structure

[0010] Referring to FIG. 1, the haptic feedback vibration motor **100** of the present invention comprises: a housing **10**, a mass block **20** disposed within an internal cavity **11** of the housing **10**, a magnet assembly **30** fixed to the mass block **20**, a first coil fixing board **40** and a second coil fixing board **50** (collectively, the "dual coil fixing boards"), a first coil **41** mounted on the first coil fixing board **40**, a second coil **51** mounted on the second coil fixing board **50**, and a plurality of elastic support members **60** connecting the mass block **20** to the housing **10**.

### Housing Structure

[0011] The housing **10** comprises an upper cover **12** and a base **13** that, when assembled, define the internal cavity **11**. In a preferred embodiment, the housing **10** is fabricated from a magnetically permeable material, such as a cold-rolled steel alloy or a permalloy composition, so as to function additionally as part of the magnetic yoke, guiding magnetic flux lines generated by the magnet assembly **30** and thereby reducing flux leakage to the exterior of the motor **100**.

[0012] The housing **10** further defines a plurality of mounting recesses **14** disposed on interior side walls thereof, configured to receive and fix the peripheral edges of the first coil fixing board **40** and the second coil fixing board **50**, respectively, such that the coil fixing boards **40**, **50** are rigidly secured in a fixed spatial relationship relative to the housing **10** and to each other.

### Mass Block and Magnet Assembly

[0013] The mass block **20** is preferably formed of a high-density material, such as tungsten alloy or a tungsten-copper composite, to maximize inertial mass within the limited spatial envelope of the motor **100**, thereby increasing the vibration amplitude achievable for a given driving force.

[0014] The mass block **20** defines a central receiving cavity **21** configured to receive the magnet assembly **30**. In the preferred embodiment, the magnet assembly **30** comprises a first magnet **31** and a second magnet **32**, each having a polarization axis oriented substantially parallel to the vibration axis X-X′, and arranged such that the first magnet **31** and second magnet **32** are stacked with opposing (or in an alternative embodiment, like) magnetic polarities facing each other, with a magnetically permeable spacer **33** disposed therebetween to concentrate and shape the magnetic flux distribution.

[0015] In an alternative embodiment, the magnet assembly **30** comprises a single unitary magnet body magnetized to form multiple poles along its length, wherein the poles are configured to align with corresponding working gaps defined between the magnet assembly **30** and the respective first and second coils **41**, **51**.

[0016] The mass block **20** further comprises side wing portions **22** extending laterally from the central receiving cavity **21**, said side wing portions **22** being connected to the elastic support members **60**, which in turn connect to anchor points **15** provided on the interior of the housing **10**, thereby suspending the mass block **20** within the internal cavity **11** and permitting reciprocating linear motion along the vibration axis X-X′.

### Dual Coil Fixing Board Structure

[0017] A principal feature of the present invention resides in the dual coil fixing board structure, which comprises the first coil fixing board **40** disposed on a first side of the magnet assembly **30** and the second coil fixing board **50** disposed on a second, opposing side of the magnet assembly **30**, such that the magnet assembly **30** is interposed between the first coil fixing board **40** and the second coil fixing board **50** along a direction substantially perpendicular to the vibration axis X-X′.

[0018] The first coil fixing board **40** and second coil fixing board **50** are each preferably formed of a rigid, non-magnetic, electrically insulating substrate material, such as a glass-fiber-reinforced epoxy laminate (e.g., FR-4) or a liquid crystal polymer (LCP), configured to provide dimensional stability under thermal and mechanical stress while preventing eddy current losses.

[0019] The first coil **41** is fixedly mounted on an inner surface of the first coil fixing board **40** facing the magnet assembly **30**, and the second coil **51** is fixedly mounted on an inner surface of the second coil fixing board **50** facing the magnet assembly **30**, such that a first working air gap **G1** is defined between the first coil **41** and the magnet assembly **30**, and a second working air gap **G2** is defined between the second coil **51** and the magnet assembly **30**.

[0020] The first coil **41** and second coil **51** are electrically connected in series or in parallel and are wound such that, upon application of an alternating driving current, the magnetic field generated by the first coil **41** and the magnetic field generated by the second coil **51** act cooperatively upon the magnet assembly **30** in the same directional sense, thereby doubling the effective electromagnetic driving force applied to the mass block **20** as compared to a single-coil configuration operating under equivalent current conditions.

[0021] This dual coil configuration further establishes a substantially closed magnetic loop: magnetic flux emanating from a first pole of the magnet assembly **30** passes through the first working air gap **G1**, through the first coil **41**, is captured by the magnetically permeable housing **10**, redirected along the housing wall, passes through the second coil **51** and second working air gap **G2**, and returns to a second pole of the magnet assembly **30**, thereby minimizing flux leakage into non-productive regions and substantially improving the magnetic efficiency, defined as the ratio of effective driving flux to total generated flux, of the motor **100**.

[0022] In a preferred embodiment, the first coil fixing board **40** and second coil fixing board **50** each further comprise a plurality of positioning studs **42**, **52** extending outward from their respective outer surfaces, said positioning studs **42**, **52** being received within corresponding positioning apertures **16** formed in the housing **10**, so as to prevent rotational or lateral displacement of the coil fixing boards **40**, **50** during motor operation and manufacturing assembly.

[0023] The dual coil fixing boards **40**, **50** further comprise electrical terminal pads **43**, **53** disposed on an exterior-facing surface thereof, electrically connected to the respective coils **41**, **51** via conductive vias or traces formed within the substrate, and configured to receive external driving current from a flexible printed circuit (FPC) **70** electrically bonded to the housing **10** or base **13**.

### Operation

[0024] In operation, an alternating current signal at or near the resonant frequency of the mass-spring system (defined by the mass of the mass block **20** and the combined stiffness of the elastic support members **60**) is applied to the first coil **41** and second coil **51** via the FPC **70**. The resultant Lorentz forces generated at both the first working air gap **G1** and second working air gap **G2** act simultaneously and cooperatively on the magnet assembly **30**, driving the mass block **20** into linear reciprocating motion along the vibration axis X-X′.
